column1: # Number agreement that is marked on the verb, not on the noun (ADR-072).
# From the field report in docs/tafsiri-swahili-numerus-fehler.md. Swahili is
# the case at hand because N-class nouns (paka, mbwa, rafiki) look identical
# in singular and plural, so the only carrier of number is the subject or
# object prefix — exactly the marking a translation can drop without leaving
# any trace in its output.
# Columns, tab separated:
#   id  sentence  expect  forbid  what it checks
# expect/forbid are extended regexes matched case-insensitively against the
# German translation, each wrapped in word boundaries by the runner. Use "-"
# for no forbid. Singular rows forbid the plural form on purpose: "Katze" is a
# substring of "Katzen", so presence alone would pass either way.
# A field may start with "cs:" to be matched case-sensitively. One row needs
# it: polite "Sie" is a correct rendering of a 2nd-person plural, while "sie"
# is the 3rd-person reading the row exists to catch, and nothing but case
# tells them apart.
# Two rows accept "ihnen" beside "Katzen". The row asks whether the plural
# survived, and "Salim hat ihnen Futter gegeben" answers yes — it drops the
# noun, which is a faithfulness fault worth its own fixture, not a number one.
obj-sg
obj-pl
perf-pl
perf-pl-pa
subj-sg
subj-pl
obj-sg-mw
obj-pl-wa
adj-sg
